page.overview:
Who is Carolina Roberta?

Carolina Roberta, known to her inner circle and posthumously more broadly by the portmaneau Caroberta (original Polish: Karolina Roberta and Karoberta), was the Duchess of Toussaint and Lady of Beauclair around the turn of the 12th and 13th century. She was the great-granddaughter of the first Lady of Beauclair, Adela Marta.

Carolina Roberta had at least one child through which she was the grandmother of the Duchess Anna Henrietta.

Holding court in the fabulous Beauclair Palace renovated on the orders of Adela Marta, the Duchess Carolina Roberta expanded the residence by adding another tower with battlements, later called the Caroberta's Tower. Moreover, she disdained it when her courtiers used knives to pick their teeth, and for that reason she introduced round ended cutlery to the palace.

Partial to the untouched wilderness of her realm, the Duchess liked to organize elaborate games with her courtiers in the forest that would, in time, be renamed Caroberta Woods. Her court included the attractive Lady Dulcinea, for whom, so it was said, duels were waged wherever she appeared; and Salvar the Lame, who was made a count in 1189 by Carolina Roberta in reward for his service to the ducal throne. Granted a silver basilisk as his heraldic beast, Salvar founded the House di Salvaress. The Duchess also employed Patrice Ludovic as the ducal hairdresser.
